## Tiwanaku excursion: the Gate of the Sun, Kalasasaya and an ancient Andean civilization

[Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/) is an archaeological site on Bolivia's high-altitude plateau near Lake Titicaca. It preserves structures built by a culture that flourished centuries before the rise of the Inca Empire. Massive stone blocks, carvings and ceremonial spaces evoke an ancient city that once served as a major political and spiritual center of the Andes.

Our itinerary includes the [Gate of the Sun](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku-gate-of-the-sun/), the [Kalasasaya temple](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku-kalasasaya/), other monumental structures and stepped pyramids. The excursion is followed by a transfer to La Paz and hotel check-in. The precise visiting time and price of the stand-alone excursion are not currently specified in our offer, so the terms of another tour should not be attributed to it.

## The Gate of the Sun: what the carvings reveal

The Gate of the Sun was carved from a single block of andesite. Its most famous feature is the relief above the opening: a central staff-bearing figure surrounded by repeated representations of people and birds. Researchers link the imagery to religious beliefs and, according to some interpretations, to a calendar cycle. There is no universally accepted interpretation of every symbol.

Take time to examine more than the main frieze: the precision of the stonework, the shape of the opening, the arrangement of figures and the carving technique are all worth noticing. These details demonstrate advanced stoneworking skills and help distinguish Tiwanaku architecture from other pre-Columbian monuments.

The [Gate of the Sun at Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku-gate-of-the-sun/) page offers more information about the monument itself. Follow the site's archaeological access rules and avoid touching protected surfaces.

## Kalasasaya and ceremonial architecture

The [Kalasasaya temple](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku-kalasasaya/) is a large rectangular complex with stone walls and monoliths. Its carefully planned geometry and the relationship between ritual architecture and views of the world are particularly striking. Together with the Gate of the Sun, Kalasasaya reveals how the ancient city's public center was organized.

UNESCO describes Tiwanaku as a powerful spiritual and political center that reached its height between approximately **AD 500 and 900**. Its inhabitants developed techniques for stoneworking, drainage construction and agriculture in harsh high-altitude conditions. These details add meaning to a visit: the ruins tell us not only about ceremonies but also about the organization of everyday life.

The excursion description also mentions stepped pyramids and monumental structures. However, the presence of a monument within the complex does not necessarily mean visitors are allowed into all its interior areas; access depends on site rules.

## How Tiwanaku differs from Inca monuments

Tiwanaku belongs to a **pre-Inca culture**. It developed long before the Inca state and had its own architectural traditions, economy and religious beliefs. Its monuments are best understood as evidence of a different stage in Andean history, rather than dismissed as “more Inca ruins.”

The route appeals to anyone interested in archaeology, the history of technology, stonework and ancient religious traditions. You could explore the region further with a separate trip to [Lake Titicaca](/bolivia/place/lake-titicaca-bolivia/), but that journey should not be assumed to be included in this excursion.

## Altitude and conditions on site

The archaeological site lies about **3850 m** above sea level. Even gentle walking can cause breathlessness for travelers who have recently arrived from lower altitudes. Allow time to acclimatize, keep a moderate pace and discuss your health and route in advance.

The plateau can be sunny, windy and cold. Bring a hat, sunglasses, drinking water, shoes suitable for uneven ground and warm layers that you can remove during the day. If your main goal is to understand the site's history, allow time for explanations and close observation rather than rushing through every stop.

## Frequently asked questions about the Tiwanaku excursion

### Are the Gate of the Sun and Kalasasaya on the same excursion?

Yes. Both monuments are included in our program. They belong to the same archaeological complex and complement each other historically.

### Did the Incas build Tiwanaku?

No. Its monuments belong to an earlier Andean culture. Many architectural and artistic features developed before the Inca period.

### Where does the itinerary go after the archaeological visit?

The program continues with **a transfer to La Paz and hotel accommodation**. The duration, price and specific services of the stand-alone excursion depend on the chosen program.

## Bolivia Dream: seeing Titicaca and the Uyuni Salt Flat in 7 days

This seven-day journey brings together Bolivia's cultural and natural highlights. Over **7 days and 6 nights**, you visit [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/), [Lake Titicaca](/bolivia/place/lake-titicaca-bolivia/), the [Island of the Sun](/bolivia/place/isla-del-sol/) and [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), along with the lagoons of the southwestern highlands.

Unlike a short jeep tour focused mainly on remote desert terrain, this journey begins and ends in La Paz. One day is devoted to Andean traditions and the lake, followed by an expedition-style road section across the salt flat and high-altitude lagoons.

## Titicaca and the Island of the Sun: the cultural part of the itinerary

Day two begins with an early departure from La Paz for [Copacabana](/bolivia/place/copacabana/) on the shore of Lake Titicaca. After crossing the Altiplano by road, the journey continues by boat to the Island of the Sun.

The itinerary includes Inca sites: the Pilkokaina Palace, the Inca Steps and the Sacred Fountain. A short uphill walk is planned near Yumani. Lunch in Copacabana, a visit to the main church and a return to La Paz follow.

This day is important for understanding local culture: [Lake Titicaca](/bolivia/place/lake-titicaca-bolivia/) is known for Andean history, religious traditions and sacred Inca sites. The journey also demonstrates the real distance between La Paz and the lake, explaining the early departure.

## Uyuni: the salt flat, Colchani and Incahuasi

On day three, travelers fly from La Paz to Uyuni. **This domestic flight is not included in the tour price.** After arrival, the program visits the Train Cemetery, [Colchani](/bolivia/place/colchani/) and its salt processing, the salt flat and [Incahuasi Island](/bolivia/place/incahuasi-island/) with its tall cacti.

The northern part of the region also includes landscapes at the foot of Tunupa Volcano. The famous mirror effect on the salt flat depends on a thin layer of water. At other times of year, the surface reveals white polygonal patterns and cracks. The season matters if you hope to photograph a particular effect, but it cannot be guaranteed for a specific date.

## Lagoons, flamingos and the Siloli Desert

The next two days cover the southwestern highlands, following a chain of volcanoes into the [Eduardo Avaroa Reserve](/bolivia/place/eduardo-avaroa-national-reserve/) and past lagoons with Andean flamingos toward the Siloli Desert.

The route includes [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), the [Sol de Mañana geysers](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/), hot springs, the Dalí Desert and [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/) near Licancabur Volcano. These natural phenomena reflect the region's volcanic history and the mineral composition of its waters.

One day begins at about **06:30**. Transfers use exposed high-altitude roads, so plan for changes in temperature, wind and possible restrictions on access to some natural sites.

## Why the journey returns to La Paz after Uyuni

On day six, travelers fly back from Uyuni to La Paz. **The return flight is also paid for separately.** After arrival, there is a city sightseeing tour and a visit to [Moon Valley](/bolivia/place/moon-valley-la-paz/) with its unusual erosion-shaped formations.

The city program includes historic squares, Killi Killi viewpoint, the Witches' Market, handicraft markets and a ride on the Yellow Line cable car with Andean panoramas. Day seven ends with an airport transfer.

The itinerary therefore combines two very different ways of traveling: comfortable city stops and several days of expedition-style travel near Uyuni. It is neither a wholly stationary vacation nor seven continuous days of driving through the desert.

## Accommodation and included services

The tour provides:

| Accommodation | Nights |
| --- | ---: |
| La Paz, Rosario Sur | 3 |
| Uyuni and the salt-flat/lagoon region | 3 |

The Uyuni section includes separate overnight stays on the salt flat, near the lagoons and in town, including Rosario Collection Uyuni. The full itinerary has **6 nights**.

**The base price is $2998.** It includes private tourist transport, English-speaking guides on excursions, entrance tickets, breakfast at every hotel, **3 lunches and 2 dinners during the Uyuni section**, and 1 lunch in Copacabana.

Airfares, meals not expressly listed, airport taxes, tips and drinks are not included. The price should therefore be considered alongside flights between La Paz and Uyuni, rather than compared only with overland jeep programs.

## Preparing for altitude and climate

La Paz, Titicaca and Uyuni are all at considerable elevations. On the plateau, acclimatization, sun protection, water and warm layers for nights are especially important. The activity involves road journeys, walks and short climbs; high altitude affects how you feel even without strenuous trekking.

If your only goal is to see lagoons and the salt flat, compare this with the [three-day jeep tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-uyuni-salt-flats-jeep-tour-3-days/). Travelers who also want to explore Tiwanaku archaeology and the natural landmarks of Torotoro may prefer the [larger eleven-day program](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-titicaca-uyuni-la-paz-11-days/).

## Frequently asked questions about the seven-day Bolivia trip

### Does the program include Lake Titicaca?

Yes. It includes a trip to Copacabana, a boat crossing to the Island of the Sun and a return to La Paz.

### Are the La Paz–Uyuni flights included in $2998?

No. Both domestic flights, outbound and return, are expressly excluded from the price.

### In which language are the excursions conducted?

The base package includes excursions with English-speaking guides.

### Will the salt flat have mirror reflections?

That depends on rainfall and the condition of the salt surface. The tour includes Uyuni but does not guarantee a particular appearance of the landscape.

## Bolivia's natural wonders in 10 days: Uyuni, Madidi and Titicaca

This **10-day, 9-night itinerary** combines [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/), the [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) Salt Flat, high-altitude lagoons, the Amazonian [Madidi National Park](/bolivia/place/madidi-national-park/) and [Lake Titicaca](/bolivia/place/lake-titicaca-bolivia/). Within a few days, travelers move from the cold, dry Altiplano to humid tropical forest before returning to high elevations.

The route is ideal for those wanting to experience Bolivia's natural diversity. The main logistical challenges are frequent flights and transfers and the need to adapt quickly to changing altitude and temperature.

## The order of regions: where the ten days take you

| Days | Area |
|---|---|
| 1 | La Paz |
| 2–4 | Uyuni and the lagoons |
| 5–8 | Rurrenabaque and Madidi |
| 9 | Titicaca and the Island of the Sun |
| 10 | La Paz, departure |

Day one features a La Paz city tour, including markets, central squares, the Basilica of San Francisco and a ride on the urban cable car. It also marks the start of acclimatization before further travel across the Altiplano.

On day two, travelers head to Uyuni. The expedition begins with the Train Cemetery and [Colchani](/bolivia/place/colchani/), then continues across the salt flat to [Incahuasi Island](/bolivia/place/incahuasi-island/) and the road toward [Tahua](/bolivia/place/tahua/). The early flight from La Paz to Uyuni **is paid for separately**.

Subsequent stages take the route through the [Siloli Desert](/bolivia/place/siloli-desert/) and high-altitude lagoons. Natural highlights include [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/) and parts of the [Eduardo Avaroa Reserve](/bolivia/place/eduardo-avaroa-national-reserve/). Both the waters' colors and the sweeping volcanic panoramas shape this region's appeal.

## How the Madidi section differs from Uyuni

From day five, the journey enters Bolivia's Amazonian region. Via [Rurrenabaque](/bolivia/place/rurrenabaque/), travelers reach [San Miguel del Bala](/bolivia/place/san-miguel-del-bala/) and [Madidi National Park](/bolivia/place/madidi-national-park/).

Here, the program revolves around tropical forest, river excursions, bird and wildlife watching, and guided walks. After the dry salt flat, conditions change completely: humidity increases, vegetation becomes dense, and travel may involve boats and walking. This is a genuine nature adventure rather than a beach vacation, and visitors must follow the rules of the protected area.

The Madidi program includes daytime and evening nature activities. Wildlife sightings cannot be guaranteed, however: they depend on weather, season and the animals' behavior. It is more useful to assess Madidi trips by the amount of time spent in the forest and the provision of guides than by promises of seeing specific species.

## The final day at Titicaca

On day nine, the route takes travelers via [Copacabana](/bolivia/place/copacabana/) to the [Island of the Sun](/bolivia/place/isla-del-sol/) and back to La Paz. This segment combines lake views, Andean cultural experiences and high-altitude roads.

After time in the Amazonian forest, the return to altitude can be particularly noticeable. Build in time for comfortable readjustment, rest and sufficient drinking water, rather than adding long walks without regard for the group's physical condition.

## Included services and important exclusions

The price includes accommodation with breakfast at the selected hotels, **private excursions and transfers**, meals specifically included in the program and the services of a **bilingual English- and Spanish-speaking guide**. This matters for Russian-speaking travelers: a Russian-speaking guide is not advertised as a standard inclusion.

**Air tickets are not included**, nor are terminal fees, optional services, extra meals and drinks, insurance, personal expenses or tips. The route uses flights between La Paz, Uyuni and the Rurrenabaque area, so those costs must be added separately when calculating the full budget.

Individual days have their own transfer and meal arrangements. These specific terms take precedence over general descriptions: do not assume every lunch over the ten days is included merely because the expedition provides some meals.

## When to travel and how to prepare

In the rainy season, Uyuni can become covered by water, creating mirror reflections. But heavy flooding makes some roads and sites less accessible. Before choosing your dates, decide whether the mirror surface or a full circuit to more distant stops matters more to you.

High humidity and rainfall in Madidi can affect river routes and forest trails. That stage calls for tropical-weather clothing and insect protection. Uyuni and the colorful lagoons require warm clothes and reliable protection from sun and wind. A single clothing set for the whole journey, without allowing for these climatic differences, is impractical.

The season and road conditions matter, but domestic flight schedules are equally important. A missed connection on such a long itinerary could reduce time in the jungle or at Titicaca, so transfers must be coordinated when arranging the trip.

## How this compares with other Bolivia tours

The [12-day journey through Samaipata, Sucre and Potosí](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-treasures-12-days/) features more colonial history and eastern Bolivian routes, but **does not include Madidi**. The shorter [seven-day La Paz–Tiwanaku–Uyuni tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-uyuni-moon-valley-la-paz-tiwanaku/) focuses on archaeology and the main highland sights without an Amazon section.

The ten-day program is a good choice when you want the salt flat, colorful lagoons and tropical forest on the same journey. See more options in the [Bolivia tours directory](/bolivia/tour/) and [nature and wildlife trips in Bolivia](/interests/wildlife/tours/bolivia/).

## Frequently asked questions about the Bolivia nature tour

### Is Madidi included in the itinerary?

Yes. Several days are allocated to the Amazonian section covering Rurrenabaque, San Miguel del Bala and Madidi.

### Are domestic flights included?

No. Air tickets appear among excluded expenses, and the itinerary expressly states that the La Paz–Uyuni flight is charged separately.

### What language are the excursions conducted in?

The list of included services specifies **bilingual English- and Spanish-speaking guidance**. Russian is not separately guaranteed.

### Are wildlife encounters in Madidi guaranteed?

No. The program includes nature excursions and wildlife observation, but the species seen and the number of encounters depend on natural conditions.

## Eleven days in Bolivia: from Tiwanaku and Titicaca to Uyuni and Torotoro

This route explores very different parts of Bolivia: the cultural sights of [Santa Cruz](/bolivia/place/santa-cruz/), the archaeological site of Tiwanaku, [Lake Titicaca](/bolivia/place/lake-titicaca-bolivia/), the [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/) region, the [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) Salt Flat and [Torotoro National Park](/bolivia/place/torotoro/).

The program spans **11 days and 10 nights**. Its defining feature is a combination of pre-Columbian history, Andean religious traditions, geological scenery, caves and traces of ancient animals. With several domestic flights and many excursions, this is a substantial expedition-style journey that deserves careful preparation.

## Tiwanaku and Titicaca: Andean history

At [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/), travelers explore the architectural monuments of a civilization that developed in the high Andes long before the Inca Empire reached its height. The complex is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Planned stops include the Gate of the Sun, the Kalasasaya temple and the Akapana Pyramid.

The journey continues to [Lake Titicaca](/bolivia/place/lake-titicaca-bolivia/). The program features a cultural village on the shore, an introduction to the crafts of Altiplano communities and a night by the lake. The following day includes a boat excursion to the Island of the Moon and the [Island of the Sun](/bolivia/place/isla-del-sol/), with sacred Inca sites, followed by travel via [Copacabana](/bolivia/place/copacabana/) back to La Paz.

This part of the trip brings archaeology together with living cultural traditions. Visits to ancient monuments and temples should not be confused with a general city tour: time is divided between transfers, crossings and walks at altitude.

## La Paz: a city on the slopes and Moon Valley

In [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/), a sightseeing tour covers urban landmarks and [Moon Valley](/bolivia/place/moon-valley-la-paz/). Erosion has sculpted the valley's softer rock into sharp spires and deep grooves.

The city itself occupies a dramatic high-altitude basin. Moving between districts provides constant views of the surrounding Andes, even on ordinary sightseeing excursions. Visitors can appreciate not only its historic landmarks but also the atmosphere of a city built among steep slopes.

## Uyuni and the colorful lagoons

The expedition portion begins with a flight to [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). Travelers visit [Colchani](/bolivia/place/colchani/) to see salt processing and [Incahuasi Island](/bolivia/place/incahuasi-island/), where cacti grow amid the white salt plain.

The route then crosses the lagoons of the high-altitude Lípez region, entering the [Eduardo Avaroa Reserve](/bolivia/place/eduardo-avaroa-national-reserve/) and reaching [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/). Other natural stops include the [Sol de Mañana geysers](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/), hot springs, the Siloli Desert and [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/).

The salt flat changes with rainfall: at times it reflects the sky like a mirror, while at others its white salt patterns are visible. No specific surface conditions can be guaranteed for your arrival date. Cold nights and lengthy transfers also need to be factored into this expedition section.

## Torotoro: caves, canyons and dinosaur tracks

The final major nature stage runs via [Cochabamba](/bolivia/place/cochabamba/) to [Torotoro](/bolivia/place/torotoro/). The park differs from Uyuni: its main attractions are canyons, caves and geological evidence of ancient life.

The itinerary lists [Umajalanta Cave](/bolivia/place/umajalanta-cave/) and [El Vergel Canyon](/bolivia/place/el-vergel-canyon/). Underground passages, stone steps and canyon-side trails call for more physical activity than simply visiting a viewpoint. Confirm the difficulty of particular sections and any age or fitness restrictions in advance.

Visits to organized routes in the park are subject to local rules, and some natural sites require an accredited guide. Guiding is included in the overall journey, but the exact format of the underground excursions should be confirmed separately.

## Excursions, meals and price

The price includes hotels, transport, overland excursions **with a Russian-speaking guide**, entrance tickets, and breakfast, lunch and dinner during the Uyuni and Torotoro sections. Dinner at Titicaca is also included.

Excluded services include additional lunches and dinners, airport taxes and tips. **The current tour description does not confirm a numerical package price**, so it would be misleading to compare it with the $2998 “Bolivia Dream” package as a more or less expensive option. An accurate quotation must reflect the chosen flights, group composition, hotels and actual itinerary version.

The travel dates in this version are **May 12–22**, but this describes a particular calendar itinerary, not confirmed departure availability in any future year. Dates and flights must be checked when arranging the trip.

## Which Bolivia itinerary should you choose?

If your main goal is lagoons, geysers and the salt flat, consider the [three-day Uyuni jeep tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-uyuni-salt-flats-jeep-tour-3-days/). The [seven-day “Bolivia Dream”](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-dream/) adds Titicaca and La Paz. The eleven-day option stands out for **Tiwanaku and Torotoro**, offering a broader historical and paleontological experience.

More journeys are available in our [Bolivia tours directory](/bolivia/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about the eleven-day trip

### Is Tiwanaku part of the main itinerary?

Yes. The archaeological complex is scheduled after Santa Cruz on the way to Lake Titicaca.

### Why does Torotoro require special preparation?

Its caves and canyons involve walking and sometimes underground passages. Difficulty and requirements depend on the specific route within the park.

### What language are the excursions conducted in?

The overall list of services specifies excursions with a Russian-speaking guide. Some individual days may mention additional guiding languages.

### How much does the eleven-day program cost?

The current description does not provide a confirmed numerical price. The amount must be calculated for the particular trip rather than assumed.

## Bolivia in 12 days: from Samaipata and cloud forest to Uyuni and Lake Titicaca

The “Treasures of Bolivia” tour connects colonial cities, pre-Columbian sites, natural parks and high-altitude landscapes. Over **12 days and 11 nights**, the route leads from [Santa Cruz](/bolivia/place/santa-cruz/) through [Samaipata](/bolivia/place/samaipata/) and [Sucre](/bolivia/place/sucre/) to [Potosí](/bolivia/place/potosi/), [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), the highland lagoons and [Lake Titicaca](/bolivia/place/lake-titicaca-bolivia/).

A distinctive feature is the changing altitude and scenery: first the warm east of Bolivia with its cloud forests, then historic Andean cities, the salt flat, the Siloli Desert and finally the shores of Titicaca and La Paz. This itinerary suits travelers who want to explore several regions and are prepared for frequent transfers.

## How the journey is organized

| Days | Main stops |
|---|---|
| 1–3 | Santa Cruz, Samaipata, Amboró |
| 4–6 | Sucre, Potosí, Uyuni |
| 7–8 | Salt flat and colorful lagoons |
| 9–10 | Copacabana, Island of the Sun |
| 11–12 | La Paz, Moon Valley |

The first day introduces the center of Santa Cruz, its markets and neighborhoods. On day two, the itinerary visits the [Samaipata archaeological site](/bolivia/place/samaipata/); day three brings [Amboró National Park](/bolivia/place/amboro-national-park/) and the Cuevas waterfalls.

El Fuerte de Samaipata is inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List. It is known for an enormous carved rock, ceremonial structures and traces of an ancient settlement. This is a fitting introduction to Bolivian archaeology before the journey reaches the highlands.

Next come [Sucre](/bolivia/place/sucre/) and the road via [Potosí](/bolivia/place/potosi/). Potosí tells a different historical story, linked to silver mining, colonial architecture and Cerro Rico mountain. This part of the itinerary reveals Bolivia through its cities and mining heritage as well as through natural scenery.

## Uyuni and the lagoons: what the highland section includes

Day seven begins the exploration of the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). Stops include [Colchani](/bolivia/place/colchani/), [Incahuasi Island](/bolivia/place/incahuasi-island/) and high-altitude roads. Incahuasi is remarkable for its large cacti and panoramic views across the salt plain.

The route then continues through the [Siloli Desert](/bolivia/place/siloli-desert/), [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) and [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), within the region of the [Eduardo Avaroa Reserve](/bolivia/place/eduardo-avaroa-national-reserve/). Dry air, sun, wind and altitude are important factors in comfort on these stages. Road conditions can also change the order of individual stops.

During the rainy season, the salt flat sometimes mirrors the sky, but this effect cannot be promised for any date. Surface conditions affect access to distant sections and islands. If Incahuasi is essential to your trip, pay particular attention to the season and whether the route can actually reach the island.

## Titicaca and La Paz at the end of the journey

After returning from Uyuni, the itinerary continues to [Copacabana](/bolivia/place/copacabana/), [Lake Titicaca](/bolivia/place/lake-titicaca-bolivia/) and the [Island of the Sun](/bolivia/place/isla-del-sol/). Here, local communities and historic monuments reveal Andean traditions against a backdrop of the high-altitude lake.

The final sightseeing stage is in [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/), including [Moon Valley](/bolivia/place/moon-valley-la-paz/). A city surrounded by mountains, houses on steep slopes and the valley's unusual erosion formations contrast sharply with the salt desert and lakeshores.

Travelers with limited time can compare this tour with the [seven-day La Paz, Tiwanaku and Uyuni journey](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-uyuni-moon-valley-la-paz-tiwanaku/). That route covers fewer regions, whereas this 12-day tour also includes Samaipata, Amboró, Sucre, Potosí and the high-altitude lagoons.

## Confirmed accommodation, meals and guiding

The program includes accommodation in the specified towns along the route, hotel breakfasts, guided excursions, transport and entrance tickets. During the Uyuni package, **breakfast, lunch and dinner** are provided. Lunches and dinners on other days should not be assumed to be included unless specifically stated.

**Air tickets**, airport taxes, tips and unspecified meals are paid for separately. The itinerary includes domestic flights, but naming a flight in the day-by-day schedule does not mean the ticket is covered by the base price. The conditions for individual hotels and transfers should be confirmed together with travel dates.

The price and detailed itinerary are available on this Ada Tours journey's page. When comparing tours, consider whether flights, meals during the lagoon expedition and guide services for different stages are included, rather than relying only on the number of days.

## Who this tour suits

The journey appeals to travelers interested in archaeology, nature and high-altitude landscapes. The main demands come from **altitude and long road journeys**, rather than mandatory sports ascents. Visiting the salt flat and lagoons calls for protection from sun, wind and cold, comfortable footwear and enough time to acclimatize.

If your main goal is the natural contrast between the highlands and Amazonian forest, explore the [10-day tour including Madidi National Park](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-natural-wonders-10-days/). For an introduction to Bolivia without a long detour through eastern and southern regions, consider the [seven-day Uyuni–La Paz–Tiwanaku itinerary](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-uyuni-moon-valley-la-paz-tiwanaku/). More options can be found in the [Bolivia tours directory](/bolivia/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about the 12-day Bolivia tour

### Are all excursions guided?

Yes. This tour's list of included services explicitly states **guide accompaniment on every excursion**. Confirm the languages and format of individual outings in the specific offer.

### Are domestic flights included?

No. Air tickets are listed among expenses excluded from the base package price.

### Does the tour visit Madidi National Park?

No. This program covers Amboró, Samaipata, Uyuni and the highland regions. Madidi features on a separate [ten-day nature itinerary](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-natural-wonders-10-days/).

### Can I see mirror reflections at Uyuni?

That depends on rainfall and the state of the salt surface. The effect cannot be guaranteed for a given date, and water may restrict access to some attractions.
